content: 1. Drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system, such as ramipril, can cause harm and even death to a developing fetus. 2. The initial dose of ramipril for patients not receiving diuretics is 2.5 mg orally once daily. 3. 4. The maintenance dose of ramipril ranges from 2.5 mg to 20 mg orally, administered once or twice daily. 5. In some patients treated with a once-daily regimen, the antihypertensive effect may diminish toward the end of the dosing interval. 6. For such patients, consider increasing the dosage or switching to twice-daily administration. 7. 8. To reduce the risk of myocardial infarction, stroke, and cardiovascular death, the recommended dosage for the first week is 2.5 mg orally once daily, followed by 5 mg orally once daily for the next three weeks, and then a maintenance dose of 10 mg orally once daily if tolerated. 9. In hypertensive or post-myocardial infarction patients, ramipril can also be administered as a divided dose. 10. 11. If possible, reduce the dose of any concomitant diuretic to decrease the likelihood of hypotension. 12. The occurrence of hypotension after the initial dose of ramipril does not preclude subsequent careful dose titration following effective management of the hypotension. 13. In patients with renal impairment (estimated creatinine clearance ≤ 40 mL/min), dosage adjustments are necessary. 14. For patients with hypertension and renal impairment, the adjusted dose is 1.25 mg orally twice daily, with a maximum dose of 2.5 mg orally twice daily, depending on clinical response and tolerability. 15. In patients with volume depletion or renal artery stenosis, initiate ramipril at a dose of 1. 16. Patients with a history of angioedema unrelated to ACE inhibitor therapy may be at increased risk of angioedema while receiving an ACE inhibitor. 17. Angioedema involving the face, extremities, lips, tongue, glottis, and larynx has been reported in patients treated with ACE inhibitors. 18. Angioedema associated with laryngeal edema can be fatal. 19. If laryngeal stridor or angioedema of the face, tongue, or glottis occurs, discontinue ramipril immediately and institute appropriate therapy. 20. In cases where airway obstruction is likely, administer subcutaneous epinephrine promptly. 21. Controlled clinical trials have shown that ACE inhibitors cause a higher rate of angioedema in Black patients compared to non-Black patients. 22. Patients taking concomitant mTOR inhibitors (e.g., temsirolimus) may be at increased risk for angioedema. 23. Intestinal angioedema has been reported in patients treated with ACE inhibitors, presenting with abdominal pain, nausea, or vomiting, and resolving after discontinuation of the ACE inhibitor. 24. In patients undergoing desensitization treatment with hymenoptera venom while receiving ACE inhibitors, life-threatening anaphylactoid reactions have occurred. 25. Anaphylactoid reactions have also been reported in patients undergoing dialysis with high-flux membranes or low-density lipoprotein apheresis with dextran sulfate absorption while on ACE inhibitors. 26. Rarely, ACE inhibitors, including ramipril, have been associated with a syndrome starting with cholestatic jaundice and progressing to fulminant hepatic necrosis and sometimes death. 27. Discontinue ramipril if the patient develops jaundice or marked elevations of hepatic enzymes. 28. Patients with impaired liver function may develop markedly elevated plasma levels of ramipril due to its hepatic metabolism. 29. Changes in renal function may occur in susceptible individuals as a consequence of inhibiting the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system. 30. In patients with severe congestive heart failure, treatment with ACE inhibitors may be associated with oliguria, progressive azotemia, acute renal failure, or death. 31. In hypertensive patients with renal artery stenosis, increases in blood urea nitrogen and serum creatinine may occur, which are reversible upon discontinuation of ramipril and/or diuretic therapy. 32. Monitor renal function during the first few weeks of therapy in patients with renal impairment or those on diuretics. 33. In rare cases, ACE inhibitors may cause neutropenia, agranulocytosis, or bone marrow depression, particularly in patients with collagen-vascular disease and renal impairment. 34. Ramipril can cause symptomatic hypotension, especially in patients who are volumeor salt-depleted due to diuretics, dietary salt restriction, dialysis, diarrhea, or vomiting. 35. Correct volume and salt depletion before initiating ramipril therapy. 36. If excessive hypotension occurs, place the patient in a supine position and, if necessary, treat with intravenous saline infusion. 37. In patients with congestive heart failure, ACE inhibitors may cause excessive hypotension, oliguria, azotemia, or acute renal failure. 38. Initiate ramipril therapy under close medical supervision in such patients and monitor closely during the first two weeks of treatment. 39. Ramipril may block angiotensin II formation during surgery or anesthesia, leading to hypotension, which can be corrected by volume expansion. 40. Use of drugs acting on the renin-angiotensin system during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy can cause fetal and neonatal morbidity and death. 41. Discontinue ramipril as soon as pregnancy is detected. 42. Dual blockade of the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system with ACE inhibitors, angiotensin receptor blockers, or aliskiren is associated with increased risks of hypotension, hyperkalemia, and renal dysfunction. 43. Avoid concomitant use of ramipril with aliskiren in patients with diabetes or renal impairment (GFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m²). 44. Hyperkalemia has been reported in approximately 1% of hypertensive patients receiving ramipril, particularly in those with renal insufficiency, diabetes, or concomitant use of potassium-sparing diuretics or supplements. 45. Persistent nonproductive cough has been reported with ACE inhibitors, resolving after discontinuation of therapy. 46. Ramipril has been evaluated for safety in over 4,000 hypertensive patients, with adverse events similar to placebo. 47. The most frequent side effects reported were headache, dizziness, and fatigue, with fatigue being more common in ramipril-treated patients. 48. Rare adverse reactions include hepatic failure, pancreatitis, angioneurotic edema, and hematologic abnormalities such as pancytopenia and thrombocytopenia. 49. Monitor renal function and serum potassium levels in patients receiving ramipril and NSAIDs, as co-administration may lead to renal dysfunction. 50. Increased serum lithium levels and symptoms of lithium toxicity have been reported with ACE inhibitors; monitor lithium levels frequently in such cases. 51. Ramipril has not been found to interact with food, digoxin, antacids, or other common medications. 52. Clinical trials have shown no evidence of tumorigenic or mutagenic effects of ramipril in animal studies. 53. Ramipril has not been associated with teratogenic effects in animal studies at doses significantly higher than the maximum recommended human dose. 54. Laboratory findings include rare increases in creatinine, blood urea nitrogen, and liver enzymes, which are usually reversible. 55. Discontinue ramipril if significant laboratory abnormalities occur.
